done_when: forge close --resolve accept applies the owner's choice when only the default branch moved or only Forge's own records changed since the stopped review (the check compares the item's own changes against the review's merge base and ignores files under .factory/); --dismiss after a recorded choice works on the same terms; a clean review clears an unanswered review-loop stop; one command test per case; skill.md says so; new and earlier-adopted client repos get it, with a command test for each

findings.body:
Stopped reviews recorded before this upgrade have `branch_diff` but no `base`: the pre-change `review.run` return shown in this patch never saved it. If the default branch advances through the reviewed commit, as test_1 exercises, this fallback selects that commit itself as the base. The saved fingerprint describes the original product diff, while the current fingerprint describes an empty product diff, so accept still refuses with `stale_choice`; dismissals after a recorded choice also fail. Likewise, an older fingerprint containing a named or cited `.factory/` file cannot match the newly filtered fingerprint, even when only Forge records changed.

The earlier-adopted tests upgrade the client before creating its stopped reviews, so they miss both cases. Preserve freshness for existing stopped reviews and add command coverage that records the review using the pre-change implementation before upgrading.
findings.title: Not done: forge close --resolve accept applies the owner's choice when only the default branch moved or only Forge's own records changed

why: The owner's review-loop choice often can't be applied: accept is refused once the default branch moves, a dismissal is refused because recording the choice counts as a change, and a hold stays after a later review comes back clean
